name: SHENG'S LAUNDRY & THE HIGH RIDGE PATH

sources: docs/05-examine-layer.md::ROOM 28 — SHENG'S LAUNDRY & THE HIGH RIDGE PATH

subjects.name: THE COPPERS
LOOK_AT: Three copper boilers at a rolling steam. Ah-Lam Sheng runs the only business in the district with repeat customers and clean margins, and the town has decided not to notice.
Each copper has its own fire and its own temper, and he knows both.
The water in the last copper is the clearest in Consolation. It has been boiled into honesty.
LISTEN_TO: Water at the boil, cloth turning in it. Industry, actually happening.
Water, and a rhythm to it. Somebody has worked out the fastest way to do this and has been doing it that way for years.
The lid on the middle copper lifting and settling, like a man about to object and deciding it is not worth it.

overrides.OPEN: Steam took my hat's shape briefly. Sheng did not look up: 'Collars are extra.'

subjects.name: THE MANGLE
LOOK_AT: A hand-cranked mangle, the single most reliable machine in the territory. It has never broken. Nobody else can say that about anything they own.
The rollers are wood, worn so smooth they shine. Ten thousand shirts have gone through them and come out flatter and better.
A brass plate on the frame gives a maker and a city. It is the only thing in Consolation that came from somewhere and still works.
LISTEN_TO: Rollers, waiting. A machine that keeps its promises keeps them quietly.
A slow creak as the crank settles back a quarter turn.
Nothing. It is resting, and it has earned it more than anyone in town.

overrides.USE: He let me turn the crank once. It was the most useful thing I have done in the territory and we both knew it.

subjects.name: THE DRYING LINES
LOOK_AT: Lines of shirts drying in ridge wind, whiter than anything else for a hundred miles. From the diggings it looks like the hillside is surrendering.
Every shirt is pegged by the tail, shoulders down, so the collar dries straight. There is a method to all of it.
My own shirt is up there, the better one. It looks more respectable on the line than it has ever looked on me.
LISTEN_TO: Cloth, filling and luffing. The hill wearing sails.
A peg snapping shut on a corner as the wind takes it.
A long gust that fills every shirt at once. A whole congregation, breathing in.

subjects.name: THE COLLAR ADVERTISEMENT
LOOK_AT: A printed advertisement for detachable collars, pinned inside the door. The gentleman modeling them is square-jawed, confident, and — I am increasingly sure — the same man as in every printed image in this town.

A portrait of a gentleman in an excellent collar, advertising the excellence of the collar. I have seen this man before. He is on the front page of the Clarion once a month and his name there is Obadiah Mott.
Up close, the printing is very fine. He has a dimple. I had not noticed the dimple in the Clarion.
LISTEN_TO: Paper on a nail. The gentleman keeps his own counsel.
Nothing.
The paper lifting at one corner when the door opens, and lying flat again.

overrides.TALK_TO: I asked the gentleman who he really was. He kept his jaw square and his counsel. He is the most consistent man in Consolation and he does not exist.

subjects.name: THE TICKET RAIL
LOOK_AT: Claim tickets on a wire, numbered in two scripts. Sheng's numbering has never once been disputed, which makes it the district's most trusted ledger.
Each ticket is torn in half. He keeps one half and you keep the other, and the two halves have never once failed to meet.
My own ticket is on the wire: one shirt, one collar. My entire wardrobe, in Sheng's custody.
LISTEN_TO: Paper tags, ticking along the wire. A small abacus of shirts.
The tags sliding as he moves a shirt along the rail.
Nothing, for a moment. The wire waiting for the next number.

overrides.PULL: The district's one uncorrupted ledger, on a wire. I withdrew my hand with the reverence it was owed.

subjects.name: THE STARCH CROCK
LOOK_AT: Starch, mixed stiff. Consolation's collars stand up straight even when their owners cannot.
There is a paddle standing upright in it, unsupported. That is how stiff it is.
He mixes it by eye and is never wrong. I tune by ear. We have a professional understanding.
LISTEN_TO: A thick, patient bubble. Rigidity, brewing.
A slow bubble breaking the surface, considering.
Nothing. Even the starch here stands to attention.

subjects.name: THE STOVE & IRONS
LOOK_AT: Flat irons in ranks on the stove top, rotated by weight and heat in an order I could not learn in a year.
Each handle is wrapped in rag of a different color, so he knows which iron is which without looking.
One iron is smaller than the rest. It is for collars, and it has done more for this town's dignity than the church.
LISTEN_TO: Iron on iron, set down and taken up. A steady percussion. It is the closest thing this town has to a metronome, and I would know.
A hiss as he tests an iron with a wet finger.
Iron set down, iron taken up. Still the steadiest time in town.

subjects.name: THE MENDING BASKET
LOOK_AT: Torn shirts awaiting needles. The territory is hard on elbows. Half the mending is the same three men's.
One shirt has been mended so often it is mostly mending. The original shirt is a rumor.
The needles are stuck in a pincushion shaped like a strawberry. It is the only frivolous object in the building.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Damage, at rest.
Nothing. Torn cloth, waiting its turn.
Nothing. The damage has been sorted by owner.

subjects.name: THE HIGH RIDGE PATH
LOOK_AT: The path up the ridge starts at the door, which is why the laundry gets the wind and the wind gets the shirts. It climbs like it means it.
The first stretch is stepped with flat stones, carefully set. Past the laundry, nobody bothered.
It climbs to the only place in the district with a view, and it starts at the only place in town that works.
LISTEN_TO: Wind, arriving from a long way off with nothing in its pockets.
Boots coming down it, slowly. Someone who went up to decide something.
The wind coming down the path, and the shirts turning to meet it.

subjects.name: THE PAYMENT TIN
LOOK_AT: Coins in a tin, exact change encouraged by a sign in two languages and one universal tone.
The sign says EXACT CHANGE, and underneath, in English only, PLEASE. The please is for the English.
He has never once counted it in front of a customer. He does not need to.
LISTEN_TO: Honest weight. It does not rattle; it is past rattling.
Nothing. Sheng's money does not discuss itself.
A coin settling as the shelf takes my elbow. One clean note, and done.

overrides.OPEN: It does not rattle and it does not open for customers. Sheng's bank has one teller and no robberies. The Company should take the tour.

subjects.name: SHENG'S CHAIR
LOOK_AT: A chair by the door, angled at the ridge, for the ten minutes a day the boilers allow. The view is the wage.
A chair by the door, facing out, worn smooth. He sits here and watches the street and everyone assumes he is resting.
A cup of tea on the floor beside it, gone cold. The ten minutes were interrupted.
LISTEN_TO: The chair is still warm-sounding, if that is a thing. The ten minutes were recent.
Nothing.
Nothing. The chair is empty, and he is at work, which is where he usually is.

subjects.name: THE WINDOW, STEAMED
LOOK_AT: The one window, permanently fogged from inside. The town appears through it as coloured weather, which flatters it.
A small clear circle is wiped in the fog at the height of a seated man. He watches the street through it.
Through the clear spot, Main Street, very small and very sharp, like a picture in a locket.
LISTEN_TO: A drop of condensation running. The window keeps time in its own way.
Steam ticking against the glass, then running.
The street, muffled to almost nothing. The coppers win.

subjects.name: THE LEDGER
LOOK_AT: Laundry accounts. And, in the same book, in the same hand, in a column headed nothing at all, rather larger numbers.
The laundry columns total to the cent. The other column totals to a great deal more than laundry.
He saw me reading it and did not close it. In this town that is a kind of respect.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Nothing. Figures that balance make no noise.
The page lifting in the steam and settling again, heavy with damp and arithmetic.

subjects.name: THE COLLARS
LOOK_AT: Two hundred collars, boxed, by name. Every important man in Consolation is in this box.
Each box is labeled with a name. The Colonel has six. The Reverend has one, very clean.
There is a box with my name on it. It holds one collar, which is the right number.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Starch is silent.
Nothing. Starch keeps a straight face.
A box lid settling. Somebody's dignity, put away for the week.

subjects.name: THE THURSDAY BOOK
LOOK_AT: A separate book for Thursdays. Thursdays appear to be different.
The entries are short: a date, a name, a sum. Every date is a Thursday.
It is shelved a hand's width from the laundry book. A hand's width is the distance between washing and banking in this town.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Nothing. Thursdays are kept quiet.
The spine creaking as I lean near it. It is not used to visitors on a Monday.

subjects.name: THE BACK ROOM
LOOK_AT: A curtain across a doorway, and behind it a room I am not invited into.
The curtain is clean. Everything here is clean, including, I suspect, the business behind it.
Once the curtain moved, and I saw a desk and a lamp and a great many papers in very good order. Then it moved back.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing behind the curtain, or nothing I am meant to hear.
A pen, somewhere back there, adding.
Nothing. Sheng's back room is where the town's noise goes to be counted.

subjects.name: THE SCALE
LOOK_AT: A brass scale for weighing laundry by the pound. It is as accurate as the one at the assay office, and it weighs shirts.
The weights are stamped and checked. A man who weighs collars this honestly would weigh anything honestly.
I put my hat on it. Eleven ounces. Sheng did not charge me.
LISTEN_TO: A small tick as the pan settles level.
Nothing. It is perfectly balanced, and has nothing to add.
The beam rocking once when the door goes, and finding level again without help.

AH-LAM SHENG.PICK_UP: He would tell me my weight to the ounce, and what I owe him for the information.
AH-LAM SHENG.PUSH: He is ironing. I value my hand.
AH-LAM SHENG.USE: Everybody in town uses Sheng. He keeps a book of it.
